facts.text: Hoonah (Tlingit: Xunaa) means 'lee of the north wind', a name that reflects the village's sheltered position.
The Huna Heritage Library holds about 250 books on Alaska Native and Tlingit culture, offering a deep dive into local history.
Huna Heritage Digital Archives hosts hundreds of images and recordings that preserve Hoonah's cultural heritage for future generations.
The former Hoonah Air Force Station now powers one of the world’s longest zip-lines, connecting the station to the historic cannery.
Clans fleeing Glacier Bay’s advancing ice settled Xunaa in the 1750s, marking the beginning of Hoonah’s modern history.
HHF stewards a diverse collection of photographs, audio, and papers that document Hoonah Tlingit language and traditions.
